title: 5.1.22 Frame Loop Writeup
description: Written reflection on setup/draw and the 60fps math. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.prompt:
Answer all three questions in a typed response.

Question 1: In your own words, what is the difference between setup() and draw() in a shplay sketch? When does each one run?

Question 2: shplay runs at about 60 frames per second. If you set player.vel.x = 4, how many pixels does the sprite move in one second? Show your math. How far in 5 seconds? If your canvas is 400 pixels wide, approximately how long until the sprite crosses the whole canvas?

Question 3: Why do you think the engine gives us vel (velocity) instead of letting us directly set pos.x every frame? Give one reason.

rubric.title: Q1: setup() vs draw() explained in your own words
rubric.description: Student clearly states setup() runs once at start and draw() runs every frame (about 60 times/sec). Bonus for mentioning setup() builds the world and draw() handles per-frame updates.

rubric.title: Q2: 60 fps math shown — 1-second and 5-second distances, canvas-crossing time
rubric.description: 4 px/frame × 60 fps = 240 px/sec. 5 sec = 1200 px. 400 px canvas / 240 px/sec ≈ 1.67 sec. Student must show at least one multiplication step — not just final numbers.

rubric.title: Q3: One sensible reason for using velocity instead of direct position
rubric.description: Any reasonable answer: lets physics/collisions integrate, smoother motion, avoids fighting the engine, frame-rate independence, etc. Looking for ONE clear reason — doesn't need to be the textbook answer.
